The investigated samples consist of a 1200 nm thick GaN buffer layer, followed by a 50 nm thin (Ga,Fe)N layer containing nanocrystals, and in some cases a 70 nm thick GaN capping layer.
HRXRD analysis identifies the presence of two crystalline phases in the nanocrystals: α-Fe and γ'-GayFe4-yN.
The size of the α-Fe nanocrystals is estimated to be 17±2 nm, while the γ'-GayFe4-yN nanocrystals are 22±2 nm along the growth direction.
The magnetic response of the samples is dominated by a superparamagnetic-like behavior and a paramagnetic contribution from dilute Fe3+ ions in the matrix.
The coercive field values observed in the samples (10-60 mT) are consistent with the presence of ferromagnetic γ'-Fe4N nanocrystals.
The FMR measurements confirm the presence of an in-plane uniaxial magnetic anisotropy in the embedded nanocrystals.
The post-growth annealing of Sample A leads to the removal of the α-Fe nanocrystals and the formation of polycrystalline FeOx at the surface.
The resistivity of the capped Sample B is enhanced by up to three orders of magnitude compared to the other samples, due to the diffusion of dilute Fe ions into the GaN capping layer.
The magnetoresistance of the samples shows a transition from Arrhenius-type conduction at high temperatures to Mott variable-range hopping at lower temperatures.
The anisotropic magnetoresistance (AMR) is observed in all samples containing the (Ga,Fe)N layers, but not in the GaN reference sample.
The hopping distance Rh is estimated to be 30-70 nm, while the localization length ξ is 7-10 nm, fulfilling the condition Rh > ξ for hopping conduction.
The hysteretic behavior in the magnetoresistance of Sample A* at low fields is attributed to the spin polarization of the embedded nanocrystals.
The estimated concentration of dilute Fe ions in the GaN matrix is less than 0.1%, suggesting that most of the Fe is incorporated into the nanocrystals.
The magnetic anisotropy of the nanocrystals, as observed in the FMR measurements, is attributed to shape anisotropy and the hexagonal crystal structure of the GaN matrix.

The positive anisotropic magnetoresistance observed in the samples containing the (Ga,Fe)N layers is not present in the GaN reference sample, indicating that it is a result of the embedded nanocrystals.
